office_does: The three county commissioners set the county budget and county taxes, oversee county roads and buildings, and run county business.
race_blurb: One-term Commissioner Jack Miller, a retired farmer who names over-taxation as residents' main problem, faces farmer, orchardist and Walla Walla Community College board chair Bill Warren, who says the county needs funds for youth, families and the planned pool. Both prefer the Republican Party; District 3 voters chose the finalists in August (Warren 215, Miller 198), and the whole county votes in November.

candidates.summary: Lifelong Columbia County farmer, orchardist and rancher, and a Walla Walla Community College trustee since 2017 and current board chair, making his first run for county office.
highlights: Says the community 'needs funds' for youth and young families: complete the pool project and maintain child care [S3]
Would maintain investments in critical infrastructure and modernize county systems [S1]
Would abide by the state's sanctuary law [S3]
Walla Walla Community College trustee since 2017, current board chair [S1]

spending.basis: Argues the community needs funds for youth and family services, completing the pool project and child care, and would maintain infrastructure investment.

experience.basis: Challenger with no county office experience who says he can 'bring a stronger voice', though he has served as a college trustee since 2017.

candidates.summary: District 3 commissioner since 2023 and a retired farmer who managed the Coeur d'Alene Tribal Farm for more than 30 years, seeking a second term.
highlights: Names 'over taxation' as the main problem for residents and backs raising the income limit for property tax exemptions [S3]
'My priority is always to maintain a positive cash flow'; pledges to spend carefully and reduce regulations [S1]
Says state sanctuary laws 'need to be abolished' [S3]
Won the seat in 2022 over incumbent Charles Amerein, 1,094 to 1,005 [S13]
Says the new-commissioner learning curve 'is now behind me' [S3]

taxes.basis: Calls over-taxation the main problem facing residents and favors widening property tax exemptions; stresses careful handling of tax dollars.

spending.basis: Priorities are positive cash flow, careful spending and spending 'as efficiently as possible', without a specific audit or cut proposal.

experience.basis: One-term incumbent running on his record and the experience he gained in office.
